content.text:
Four of five readers finished; the fifth (browser tests and docs) hit the usage limit, so I cover that group from this session's own gate runs and mark it as not independently re-read. I verified the load-bearing findings myself against the code before reporting them.

---

# Explain-diff: `feature-ultra` (PR #11), 1 commit, `main...HEAD`

## 1. TL;DR

Makes the workflow's independent reviewer a real, attachable Claude session and surfaces its verdict plus the run's assignment in the Projects viewer. Blast radius is the whole stack: the Python controller (`workflow/`), both contracts, the Fastify adapter, the React viewer and all their tests, 56 files, +6,074/-333. Roughly 60% of the insertions are tests and fixtures.

Confidence: **high on the happy paths** (offline suites, both browser phases and four live reviewer sessions exercised them), **medium on recovery paths** (several interrupt/failure branches are tested only through fakes that cannot reach the guard they claim to cover). No P0 or P1 findings survived verification; eleven P2s below.

## 2. Change map

| Area | Files | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| Reviewer session (slice A) | `workflow/automatic.py`, `interactive.py`, `pipeline.py`, `launch.py`, `contracts/workflow/reviewCompletion.schema.json` | Launch, wait for, validate and stop a native reviewer; print fallback behind a flag |
| Export format | `workflow/export_state.py` | `run-state.json` 1.2.0 gains `review` and `inputs` sections |
| Re-export CLI | `workflow/pipeline.py` (`ExportRuntime`, `export_run`, `export` action) | Rebuild an old run's export without launching anything |
| Contracts | `contracts/projects/v1.ts`, `examples.ts`, `contract.test.ts`, 2 generated schemas, `README.md` | `reviewResult` and `runInputs` payloads at 1.2.0 |
| Adapter | `server/projects.ts`, `projectRoutes.ts` | Validate and project the two sections; two new routes; diff artifact; snapshot changes |
| Viewer | `src/projects/{ReviewDetail,WorkerInputs,Assignment}.tsx` (new), `RunView`, `NodeDetail`, `api`, `status`, `panels`, CSS | Review panel, Assignment tab, worker input panels, finding-to-task links |
| Tests | `workflow/test_*.py` (+`test_export.py`), `server/projects.test.ts`, `tests/project-workflows/*` (+3 files) | 65 new Python tests, 8 new adapter suites, 9 new browser scenarios |
| Feature dirs and docs | `features/review-result/`, `features/run-inputs/`, RUNBOOK, 4 READMEs, 5 PRD/handoff docs | Launchable assignments; protocol and format documentation |

## 3. Walkthrough

**Reviewer as a native session.** `InteractiveSessions` learns a third node, `review` (`interactive.py:23,37-44`). `run_reviewer` (`:191-227`) launches `claude --bg` in `<run>/review-worktree` with `--tools Read,Glob,Grep,Write --allowedTools Edit(//<run>/review.completion.json) --add-dir <run> --permission-mode dontAsk`, then the prompt. The worker launch body was split into `reconcile()`/`launch()` so both share the settle-and-bind logic. Workers also now record `<node>.prompt.txt` (`:181-182`), which slice C displays.

**Completion protocol.** The reviewer reports only through a file. `read_review_completion` (`automatic.py:181-201`) refuses symlinks, oversized files, schema violations and any mismatch of run, node, launch token, bundle digest or candidate commit. `wait_review` (`:204-226`) polls until the session is idle or done with the file present, counting a deadline from the launch receipt. A native `blocked` state means "needs a human", logged once and waited through, unlike workers where it is fatal (`:117-118` versus `:219-223`).

**Lifecycle and resume.** `review_candidate` (`:229-266`) branches on the persisted receipt: succeeded (retry an unconfirmed stop, return the review), running and native (rebind the session, keep waiting), anything else refuses. `_accept_native` (`:326-364`) re-checks identity, independence, worktree and evidence before `_decide` writes `review.json` for every verdict, then stops the session. Ctrl-C leaves the receipt at `running`; the mechanism is that langgraph commits task errors only under `except Exception`, so a KeyboardInterrupt inside the node leaves the checkpoint clean.

**Export 1.2.0.** `review_section` (`export_state.py:71-90`) derives transport, reviewer, timestamp, findings and the diff hash from `review.json` plus receipts; `inputs_section` (`:141-155`) pins feature, branch, mode, automatic settings, setup, attempt cap and per-worker task, prompt, ownership, checks and four receipts. `workflow export <run>` (`pipeline.py:443-452, 635-640`) rebuilds this for an old run using a runtime that constructs no sessions, so a copied directory whose worktrees are gone still exports.

**Adapter.** Export versions 1.0.0/1.1.0/1.2.0 are accepted with strict section schemas (`projects.ts:66-141`). Projection redacts paths, bounds text at 65,536 units, computes `requirement_found_in` by verbatim substring, and registers `review.diff` as artifact `patch-review-<sha12>` served only when hash and byte length match. The review node gets its session and `result_uri` from the section alone, never from `values` (`:868-872`). Two behaviour changes apply to all nodes: `interrupted` maps to `paused`, and only status-bearing events move a node's last status (`:47-51, :841-842`).

**Viewer.** The review node renders verdict, reviewer with transport wording, bundle linked to the candidate node, a one-line summary, findings grouped by disposition or worker, and the diff link. The run gains a Run/Assignment tablist and header facts. Worker nodes gain Task (Rendered/Source with quote highlight), Exact prompt, Launch receipt, Reported-by-worker, Handoff-when-different and a stop line. Finding quotes navigate to the worker's task and mark the quote.

## 4. Decisions and assumptions the AI made

These are the choices a reviewer would not see from the diff shape:

1. **The completion file binds a controller-issued `launch_token`, not the session UUID** the PRD table names (`automatic.py:294`). The UUID does not exist when the prompt is composed; session identity is enforced separately at acceptance from `claude agents --json`.
2. **The reviewer gets the `Write` tool.** The PRD said Read/Glob/Grep only, but a file must be produced. The single-file restriction rests entirely on `Edit(//path)` semantics measured live; the repo test pins only the argv spelling (`test_interactive.py:237-241`).
3. **`review.attempt` is hard-coded to 1** (`export_state.py:88`). One review per bundle by design, so `/reviews/2` is always a 404.
4. **`transport` is inferred from file existence, not the receipt's own `transport` field** (`export_state.py:62-68`).
5. **`inputs.mode` comes from the presence of `plan.automatic`**, never from `plan.mode`, which `prepare` always sets to `interactive`.
6. **An "approved" verdict carrying an unresolved P0/P1 is persisted as `blocked`** (`automatic.py:280-282`); the reviewer's raw decision survives only in `automatic-review.json`.
7. **A completion file that fails validation once is terminal.** The live session is never asked to rewrite it. This cost a live run when a reviewer invented severity `P3`.
8. **`requirement_found_in` ignores `finding.worker`** (`projects.ts:397-406`). A quote present in both tasks yields two links; a quote the reviewer attributed to the adapter but that only exists in the UI task links to the UI task.
9. **Sections are projected eagerly, so one bad section 500s the whole workflow listing** (`projects.ts:690-710`), not just that run.
10. **`redactPaths` masks anything path-shaped, including API routes.** A task quoting `/api/projects/...` is served with `<path>` in its place.
11. **Worker lanes are hard-coded to `ui`/`adapter`** in the adapter (`projects.ts:141`) although the policy schema allows any node id.
12. **Tab, group-by and Rendered/Source are local state, not in the URL.** Header Refresh resets them.
13. **Required checks match executed checks by exact command string** (`WorkerInputs.tsx:91`), because executed checks carry no id.
14. **`stop.confirmed_at` is the stop file's mtime** (`export_state.py:121`), not a recorded timestamp.
15. **Preflight still demands the print-mode CLI flags** even for native runs (`pipeline.py:590-593`).

## 5. Risks and findings

No **P0**. No **P1**. Eleven **P2**, each verified against the code:

*Controller and export*
- `RUNBOOK.md:194` claims legacy plans "never launch a new reviewer"; nothing enforces it. `reviewer_transport()` returns `native` for a plan without the key and `review_candidate` would launch one. Only the finished project-workflows-001 is legacy, so this is a misleading doc rather than a live hazard.
- Only `KeyboardInterrupt` converts a launch-window failure into a resumable `running` receipt (`automatic.py:301-315`). A SIGHUP from a dropped SSH session leaves `needs_reconciliation` and the documented recovery is a whole new run, although the session is bindable.
- Acceptance requires the reviewer row to still be listed (`:216-218, :332-335`). An operator who exits the pane after the file is written loses a valid verdict.
- `review_section` reads `review["findings"]`, `["reviewer"]` and four more keys unguarded (`export_state.py:86-90`). A hand-edited `review.json` raises `KeyError` inside `report()`, which runs at every CLI boundary, instead of the "malformed means null" promise in the module docstring.
- `recorded_transport` reports `print` for a legacy plan whose native launch failed before writing its interactive receipt.
- `features/run-inputs/README.md:34` documents the seeded shape without the `null` transport case the adapter must accept.
- A late `attach` calls `locate(REVIEW, …)` unguarded after panes exist (`interactive.py:335`), so an unattachable reviewer row can wedge the mapping; workers check before creating anything.

*Adapter*
- Redaction has no allowlist, so API routes inside task text and finding quotes render as `<path>`. Links still resolve (matching runs on raw text), but the visible quote is not what the reviewer wrote.
- Every run-list request now projects and validates both sections for every run, with no caching. The earlier reviewer already flagged per-request packet loading here.

*Viewer*
- Both tabs set `aria-controls`, but only the selected panel is rendered, so the inactive tab points at nothing (`RunView.tsx:131` versus `:142-145`).
- Tab state does not follow route changes: browser Back from the Assignment tab, or a pasted `/nodes/<id>` URL while Assignment is open, leaves the node detail hidden.
- A pending highlight is cleared only by `TaskPanel`'s mount effect, so if the target node's inputs never load the quote survives to a later unrelated visit.
- `WorkerInputs.tsx:100` captions a failed result fetch "No published result to compare against", which asserts absence rather than failure.
- The handoff section prints "differs from what the worker reported" even when there is no completion signal at all (`:155-156`).
- A failed inputs request renders two `role="alert"` panels, one in the header and one on the worker node.

## 6. What was not done

- **The feature runs.** PRD slices B and C specified two automatic feature runs; the code was written directly instead. `features/review-result/` and `features/run-inputs/` exist and validate, and `launch --dry-run` plans them, but they were never executed.
- **No operator reconcile path for a reviewer.** `pipeline.py:686-694` still covers `launch_*` only; recovery from `needs_reconciliation` is "stop it and start a new run".
- **PRD_REVIEWER_PANE open question left open:** failing earlier than the deadline when the reviewer idles without a file.
- **The live run is not re-exported.** project-workflows-001 is still at export 1.0.0, because re-exporting before the merge would break the `main` viewer.
- **No fuzzy requirement matching**, by decision: the live reviewer's quotes matched 8 of 8 verbatim.
- **Untested UI states:** `task-highlight-missing`, `worker-inputs-unmatched`, `launch-none`, `task-truncated`, the unscoped review link and the unscoped diff message have no browser coverage.
- **Reviewer findings on earlier code left alone.** Both reviewers flagged P2s on the already-merged viewer (event normalisation, attempt numbers, redaction in `projectWorkerResult`); they are listed in the handoff, not fixed.

## 7. What to verify

```bash
cd ~/dev/md-manager-ultra
~/dev/md-manager/.venv/bin/python -m unittest workflow.test_automatic workflow.test_interactive \
  workflow.test_feature_launch workflow.test_sessions workflow.test_verification \
  workflow.test_pipeline workflow.test_graph workflow.test_export      # expect 124 OK, ~220 s
npm run test:contracts && npx --no-install tsx --test server/projects.test.ts   # 13 and 30
npx --no-install playwright test --config=tests/project-workflows/playwright.config.ts
WORKFLOW_VERIFICATION_PHASE=candidate npx --no-install playwright test \
  --config=tests/project-workflows/playwright.config.ts                # 15 each, run one at a time
npm run build && npm run lint && git diff --check
```

Then eyeball the five judgement calls the tests cannot settle for you:

1. `server/projects.ts:397-406` against `contracts/projects/README.md:48`: do you accept lane links that ignore `finding.worker`?
2. `server/projects.ts:690-710`: do you want one malformed section to 500 the entire workflow list?
3. `workflow/automatic.py:225,347-356`: is a single invalid completion file the right place to end a run, or should the reviewer get a second chance?
4. `workflow/RUNBOOK.md:194` against `automatic.py:58-60`: the legacy-plan claim is not enforced.
5. In the running app (already up on http://127.0.0.1:5175): open the Assignment tab, press browser Back, and confirm the tab does not follow.

## 8. Understanding check

- *Why can a controller Ctrl-C during the review be resumed, but a dropped SSH session cannot?* Only `KeyboardInterrupt` is converted to a `running` receipt; a signal-killed process leaves `needs_reconciliation`, which refuses forever (`automatic.py:301-315, :242`).
- *What stops a second reviewer from ever being launched?* Four independent guards: an existing `automatic-review.json`, an existing `review-worktree`, an existing `review.interactive.json`, and a launch-name collision check (`automatic.py:234-266`, `interactive.py:199-208`).
- *Why does project-workflows-001 show "No review recorded" even though its `review.json` exists?* Its export is still version 1.0.0 and the adapter reads only the export's `review` section, never `values`. `workflow export` fixes it.
- *When does a finding quote become a link?* When it appears verbatim in a lane's raw task text **and** survives in the truncated, redacted text the API serves (`projects.ts:397-406`).

1	# Handoff: review visibility and run inputs (PRD_REVIEW_VISIBILITY, slices A, B, C)
2	
3	Implements `docs/PRD_REVIEW_VISIBILITY.md` and its three slice PRDs on branch `ultra` (worktree `~/dev/md-manager-ultra`), 2026-09-21. All three slices were implemented directly in this checkout rather than as feature runs; the feature directories `features/review-result/` and `features/run-inputs/` and the `launch` choices the PRDs ask for exist, so the runs can still be launched, but nothing in the tree depends on them. Commits are left to the user. Section 6 lists what was deliberately not done.
4	
5	## 1. What changed, by slice
6	
7	### Slice A: reviewer as an attachable native session (`workflow/`, `contracts/workflow/`)
8	
9	- `contracts/workflow/reviewCompletion.schema.json`: the reviewer's completion file (`version`, `run_id`, `node_id: "review"`, `launch_token`, `bundle_sha256`, `candidate_commit`, `verdict`, `findings[]` with `severity`, `message`, `disposition`, `worker` (`ui|adapter|both|none`) and `requirement` (verbatim quote or null)).
10	- `workflow/interactive.py`: `InteractiveSessions` knows the reviewer as node `review` (`launch_name` `workflow-<run>-reviewer`, `node_worktree` = `<run>/review-worktree`, `locate`/`settle` reused); `run_reviewer()` launches `claude --bg` with tools Read, Glob, Grep, Write, permission mode `dontAsk`, `--allowedTools Edit(//<run>/review.completion.json)`, `--add-dir <run>`, writes `review.interactive.json`, `review.prompt.txt`, `review.launch.log`; workers now also get `<worker>.prompt.txt`. `attach_panels` adds a third pane when the reviewer exists; `attach_reviewer_panel` adds it to an existing tab (split right of the adapter pane, label `Claude: reviewer`); `attach-one --node review`.
11	- `workflow/automatic.py`: `reviewer_transport` setting (`native` default, `print` fallback; plans pinned before the setting validate as native); `review_candidate` dispatches to `_review_native` (launch, `wait_review`, `read_review_completion` with schema validation and run/token/bundle/candidate binding, identity/independence/worktree/evidence re-checks, `review.json` for every verdict, identity-checked stop) or `_review_print` (the previous headless job, now also recording `worker`/`requirement`). Resume: a receipt at `running` re-enters `wait_review`; `KeyboardInterrupt` leaves the reviewer running. A native session in state `blocked` (needs a human in its pane) keeps the wait going until the deadline; no second reviewer is ever launched.
12	- `workflow/pipeline.py`: `launch_reviewer` (events with the reviewer UUID, best-effort pane), `stop_session`/`stop_reviewer` (generalised from `stop_workers`), `check_review`/`blocking_findings` (findings may carry `worker`/`requirement`; `require_approved=False` for export), `--reviewer-transport` at `prepare`, `ExportRuntime`/`export_run` and the `export` CLI action.
13	- `workflow/launch.py`: features `project-workflows`, `review-result`, `run-inputs`; `--reviewer-transport`; `--run-id` defaults to `<feature>-001`.
14	- Docs: `workflow/RUNBOOK.md` ("Automatic mode: the review step", resume path for the reviewer transcript, `workflow export`), `features/project-workflows/README.md` (new files, export 1.2.0 seam), `workflow/README.md`, `contracts/workflow/README.md`.
15	
16	### Slice B: review verdict and findings in the viewer (`contracts/projects/`, `workflow/export_state.py`, `server/`, `src/projects/`)
17	
18	- Contract 1.1.0/1.2.0: `reviewResult` (`.../runs/{run}/reviews/{attempt}`) in `contracts/projects/v1.ts` with `validateReviewResult`/`isBlockingFinding`, generated `reviewResult.schema.json`, fixtures and negative tests in `examples.ts`/`contract.test.ts`, README "Versions" section.
19	- Export 1.2.0 (`workflow/export_state.py`): `review` section from `review.json` plus the reviewer receipt (transport, session, `reviewed_at`, `review.diff` hash and size); `workflow export <run>` rebuilds `run-state.json` for old runs.
20	- Adapter (`server/projects.ts`, `server/projectRoutes.ts`): accepts export versions 1.0.0/1.1.0/1.2.0, projects the section (redaction, diff registered as artifact `patch-review-<sha12>` with hash and size checks), review node gets `session_id`/`result_uri`; 404 `REVIEW_NOT_FOUND` for runs without the section; strict section validation (`RUN_STORAGE_INVALID`, never a path).
21	- UI: review panel on the review node (verdict pill, reviewer session and transport, bundle hash linked to the candidate node, summary line, findings grouped by disposition, "Diff the reviewer saw"), "no review recorded" for legacy runs; mocks (worker phase) and seeds (candidate phase); scenarios `review-verdict`, `review-blocked`, `review-legacy`, `paths-redacted`.
22	
23	### Slice C: run inputs and finding-to-task links
24	
25	- Contract 1.2.0: `runInputs` (`.../runs/{run}/inputs`) and `requirement_found_in` on review findings (the lanes whose task text contains the quote verbatim; the adapter never guesses).
26	- Export: `inputs` section from `plan.json`, `policy.json`, launch receipts, completion signals, handoffs, stop files and the recorded prompts.
27	- Adapter: `.../inputs` route, redaction, 64 KiB truncation with a marker, timestamps normalised to `Z`, `INPUTS_NOT_FOUND` for runs without the section, verbatim quote lookup against the raw task text.
28	- UI: Assignment tab and run-header facts, worker node panels (Task with Rendered/Source toggle and highlight, Exact prompt, Launch receipt, Reported by the worker, Handoff as accepted, Stop confirmation), finding quotes linking to the worker's task scrolled to the highlighted quote; scenarios `run-assignment`, `worker-inputs`, `finding-to-task`, `inputs-legacy`, `inputs-paths-redacted`.
29	
30	## 2. How it was built and audited
31
